doc: THE single normaliser spec shared by the Zeebe capture harness (formal/traces/capture, Java) and the nano differential runner (engine-core/tests/zeebe_traces.rs, Rust). Both sides first produce RAW records shaped like Zeebe's record JSON ({recordType, valueType, intent, rejectionType, value:{...}}) and then apply exactly this spec: (1) a COMMAND_REJECTION record becomes {recordType, valueType, intent, rejectionType} in the trailing rejection lane; (2) an EVENT record whose valueType has a lane and whose intent is listed becomes {valueType, intent, <fields from value, absent -> null>}; (3) everything else (commands, unlisted value types/intents) is dropped; (4) the step's records are the lanes concatenated in the order below, each lane keeping its relative order (interleaving ACROSS lanes is not compared); (5) RUNTIME IDENTITY IS KEPT, CANONICALLY: after the projection, every field whose name ends in `Key` (record keys and the value's processInstanceKey / flowScopeKey / scopeKey / jobKey / ...) is rewritten to a canonical id — the first distinct raw key the SCENARIO's kept records touch (in step order, then lane order) becomes 1, the next 2, and so on, with the map kept for the WHOLE scenario (reset only between scenarios, never between steps — a per-step reset hides a cross-step target swap: updating either of two same-process instances would renumber to the same step-local ids). Within one record the `*Key` fields are visited in SORTED field-name order, so both implementations assign the same ids regardless of their JSON object iteration order. Raw key VALUES are engine-specific, but the identity pattern is behavioural: completing a task in instance A must not read as completing it in instance B. See formal/traces/README.md.
